LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 7.1.2 LISTENING COMPREHENSION : LISTENING FOR DETAILS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Listening and Speaking 7.1.2 Listening Comprehension : Listening for Details
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 7.1.2 Listening Comprehension : Listening for Details, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: however, on the other hand; - illustration such as for example, for instance, such as, 1. How can you tell the key information from a listening text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 7.1.2 Listening Comprehension : Listening for Details together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: A learner listens for detail, thus making them confident in note-taking skills.

● Communication and collaboration: A learner role-play and make oral presentations. This enhances the learner’s

ability to listen keenly.

Values:
Patriotism: A learner listens to texts on natural resources, thereby developing a sense of belonging.

Link to other subjects:

● Social studies provide the context from which the listening texts on Natural resources and forests can be obtained.

● German, French, Chinese, and Arabic require note-taking as part of the listening skill.

  -  Learners are guided to discuss

the kinds of details one should

look out for from a text. The

details could include numbers,

figures, points, facts, examples,

people, places, behaviour, and

opinions.


  -  Learners are guided to listen and

note the clues signaling details

from a peer.


  -  Learners are guided to listen to a

live or recorded oral presentation

on a pertinent and contemporary

issue such as natural resources,

for example, forests, and take

specific details.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to

role-play, in turns, oral

presentations in pairs as the

partner takes notes.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to

compare the notes, then revise

and display them for review.
